clue.text: Look up plastic surgery procedure

parts.note: a look or expression is what your face wears
to lift something is to move it up

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and research a cosmetic operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' reads as one phrasal verb, but it splits into two words that each give half.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a cosmetic operation that tightens the skin of the face.

clue.text: Fine steak's year out of date

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
rump is a cut of steak
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A good steak turns out to be a year past its use-by date.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpy describes clothes or style that is dowdy and old-fashioned.

clue.text: One of the party-givers gets house to split the expense

indicators.note: one thing splitting another sits inside it, breaking it into two parts

parts.note: expense means cost
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: One of a party's hosts gets the household to share what it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: The short abbreviation for house goes into the middle of the word for expense.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-host shares the role of hosting an event with someone else.

clue.text: Hung around as directed to catch yobbo

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it within, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to direct is to lead
a yobbo is a lout or oaf

explanation.surface: Someone loitered as they had been told to, in order to nab a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: A yobbo is British slang for a loutish young man.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to idle or loiter, which is what hanging around means.

clue.text: Exuberant fellow's hit with youth worker

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
to lam is to thrash or hit
a boy is a youth
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A lively man has been struck by someone who works with young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth worker' looks like a job title, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant means showy and full of exuberant flair.

clue.text: Supplies online jokes?

parts.note: E- is the prefix for electronic or online, as in email
quips are witty jokes

explanation.surface: A question about whether internet humour provides something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplies' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to provide them with what they need, so equips is a verb meaning supplies.

clue.text: Queen's article on heartless milk producer causes delicate situation

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: Q is an abbreviation for queen
an is the indefinite article
a dairy produces milk

explanation.surface: The monarch's piece about a dairy farm with no heart makes for an awkward situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a dilemma, an awkward state of uncertainty.

clue.text: Operational cut in Civil Service housing unit no one backed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: housing something means giving it a home inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a unit

indicators.note: going backwards means the words no one are read from right to left

parts.note: NO plus I for one

explanation.surface: A cut made inside the Civil Service, to a department that nobody supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operational' points to a surgical operation, not to the running of the Civil Service.
explanation.definitionFit: An incision is the cut a surgeon makes during an operation.

clue.text: Most serious cryptic setters assume name

indicators.note: to assume is to take on or take in, so the letters take an extra one inside
something cryptic is mysterious and obscured, so the letters are disguised by rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Crossword compilers take on a pseudonym and are the grimmest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Cryptic setters do work under assumed names, which gives the surface its plausibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternest is the superlative of stern, meaning severe or most serious in manner.

clue.text: Paul puzzle containing coarse detail causes commotion

indicators.note: containing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
to puzzle a name is to jumble it into a riddle, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: de-tail means removing the tail, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: coarse or heavy, as of crude features or fabric

explanation.surface: A crossword by Paul, a Guardian setter, with vulgar content, provokes an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is a real Guardian setter, so 'Paul puzzle' reads as one of his crosswords; 'detail' is to be read as de-tail.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent disturbance or upset, a commotion.

clue.text: Ungainly cowboy almost on horse at last

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of horse

explanation.surface: A clumsy cowboy only just manages to get on his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward and lacking grace, which is a sense of ungainly.

clue.text: Yard's pursuing press about keeping a note for witness

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after the rest
keeping something means holding it within, so the extra letters go inside
knocked about means the letters are thrown around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is a musical note
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard chases the press, who are holding back information from a witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard's' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police, but it is only the abbreviation; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A passer-by is someone who happens to be present and sees an event, an incidental witness.

clue.text: Peculiar boy becomes favourite to win

parts.note: peculiar means odd
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An unusual lad turns out to be the one tipped for victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes a betting favourite, rated more likely than not to succeed.

clue.text: Tidy up for artist in small, tight space

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another word

parts.note: taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A painter has to put things in order inside a cramped little room.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist sits inside the word tight just after its first letter. An en is a printing measure of space, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten a room is to put it in order, a synonym of tidy up.

clue.text: Strange modus operandi involving unknown rites troubled us

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for modus operandi

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Odd methods involving secret rituals that disturbed us.
explanation.walkthrough: The method abbreviation wraps an algebraic unknown plus the reworked rites, then us follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysterious means puzzling and hard to explain, which is to say strange.

clue.text: Sail away with me after day in the country

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the first one

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
a jib is a triangular sail
away from home means out
I is what me becomes as a subject

explanation.surface: An invitation to go sailing with the speaker after a day spent in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sail away' reads as one phrase, but it splits into a kind of sail and a word for away.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Owned up to being mad about IT man

indicators.note: turned about means the letters are moved round into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone confessed to being furious with the computer support person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT man' looks like the office tech person, but it splits into IT and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess or admit it, so admitted fits.

clue.text: A tired Mum organised day out with young

indicators.note: organised means put into a new arrangement
out means left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: An exhausted mother arranges an outing with her little ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day out' looks like a family trip, but it means remove the letter for day from the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Immature means not yet fully grown or developed, as the young are.

clue.text: Critical note hidden in prison food isn't half-eaten

indicators.note: something hidden in another sits inside it
what is eaten goes inside, so the short piece sits within the food word

parts.note: jug is slang for prison
D is a musical note
a meal is food

indicators.note: only half the word is used, so its first half is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A tip-off about prison food that has gone only half-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: A note goes inside jug; the second half of isn't goes inside meal. Jug is old British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Judgmental means quick to criticise others, which is a sense of critical.

clue.text: Call doctor to work on hip

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
op is short for opus, a musical work
hip and in both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: Summon a physician to operate on someone's hip joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' looks anatomical beside a doctor, but it means fashionable. 'On' just places it after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone casually is to drop in, so call works as the verb.

clue.text: Forbids part of family's move to Essex

parts.note: surface padding only: it sets the scene and supplies no letters

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following words is used

parts.note: found spanning these words

explanation.surface: Someone vetoes a relative's plan to relocate to Essex, a county east of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family's' is just surface padding; the letters run across move, to and Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to forbid it, so vetoes matches forbids as a verb.

clue.text: Flag poles positioned in time to follow president

indicators.note: to follow means this group comes after the first letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for president

indicators.note: positioned in means placed inside another word

parts.note: an eon is a long age of time
N for north, a pole, twice

explanation.surface: Flagpoles are set up in time for the president's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, often flown from a lance or mast.

clue.text: Check speech for wedding

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: bridal means for or of a wedding

indicators.note: speech means what is heard, not the written word

parts.note: to bridle is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: An instruction to proofread the toast to be given at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check speech' reads as reviewing a best man's toast; check is really the verb restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal means relating to a bride or wedding, as in bridal wear.

clue.text: Upset by a horse on short course catching fence finally

indicators.note: catching means trapping something inside
short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
gee-gee is a childish word for horse
a watercourse

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of fence

explanation.surface: Distressed by a horse on a shortened racecourse catching the last fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a racecourse beside a horse and fence, but it is a watercourse, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to distress or wrong someone, to upset them.

clue.text: Inner core of junta regret being disloyal

indicators.note: the inner core means only the middle letters, without the outside ones

parts.note: the inside letters of junta
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: The inner circle of a military regime repent of treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue can mean unfaithful, as in a false friend, which is a sense of disloyal.

clue.text: Retire from stage, depressed

parts.note: a stage in a process is a step
feeling down is feeling depressed

explanation.surface: An actor quits the theatre, feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire from stage' reads as an actor quitting; the stage is a step, not a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to resign or withdraw from a post, a sense of retire.

clue.text: Really popular act

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A performer's turn that is genuinely well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic word meaning truly or really.

clue.text: Together as part of a trade union

parts.note: being part of something is being in it
Unison is a large British public-sector trade union

explanation.surface: Working together as fellow members of a union.
explanation.walkthrough: Unison is the name of a big British union for public-service workers, so being in it is being in the union.
explanation.definitionFit: In unison means acting or speaking simultaneously, in agreement, which is together.
